transportNote: No ethernet cables were available, so the two gateway links are USB CDC/RNDIS gadget functions on the Cat2 instead of eth0/eth1. The Cat2 is still a physically separate dual-NIC gateway in series; L2 bridging, gate membership, PID1 lease, auth and fault behaviour are all hardware-real on the Cat2. Ethernet-PHY-specific items (1000Mb/s duplex, VLAN tag forwarding, PHY flap) are NOT_RUN. See protocol/TRANSPORT-SUBSTITUTION.md.

cat2.serverTransport: USB RNDIS gadget function rndis.usb1 (host MAC 02:11:11:11:11:01)
cat2.uplinkTransport: USB RNDIS gadget function rndis.usb2 (host MAC 02:22:22:22:22:01)
cat2.managementChannel: USB RNDIS rndis.gs0 (out-of-band, independent of br0/usb1/usb2)
cat2.ethernetPortsRole: NOT_USED this run (no cables); available for a future Ethernet-transport replication

protectedHost.implementation: network namespace 'victim' on the operator laptop (stronger no-bypass property than the whole laptop: the namespace contains ONLY agvictim0)
protectedHost.upstreamInterface: aguplink0 (02:22:22:22:22:01) on the laptop host, NAT-ed to wlo1

upstream.internetProbe: 223.5.5.5 / 1.1.1.1:443 (verified reachable through the gate during release)
